name: Diet diaries
desc: Dietary data had been collected at ages 4, 36, 43 and 53 years. At age 4 years, a brief 24 hour dietary recall was conducted to mothers of the cohort members. In adulthood, an estimated (unweighed) diet diary was used. At ages 36 and 43 years, this consisted of 2 days of recall and 5 days of prospective recording; at age 53 years only the 5 days of prospective recording was collected, and in general the 5 days of prospective recording have been used in publications of dietary data from all adult timepoints much more frequently than the 2 days of recall

name: Saliva assays
desc: This category contains information on the assays that have been performed on the 1946 birth cohort saliva samples and their results.Survey members attending the clinic were asked to provide a saliva sample at the clinic and then three further samples (at 9.00-9.30pm the evening they attended clinic and then on waking the following morning and again at 30 minutes after waking). Survey members were asked to put their evening sample in the green coloured tube, their waking sample in the yellow coloured tube and their waking + 30 sample in the red coloured tube. Where they used the incorrect colour, the order of the cortisol readings was amended. The correct final sequence for the four cortisol samples is waking, waking + 30, clinic sample, evening sample. Note that the clinic and evening samples were collected the day before the waking and waking + 30 samples.

name: Blood pressure
desc: This category contains information on blood pressure measurements systolic/diastolic and pulse rate using the Omron digital blood pressure monitor. Mean arterial pressure and derived hypertension variables are also available. Information was also collected on the willingness of participant to have blood pressure measured. Some or all of these measures are available in 1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years), 2015 (age 69 years) and 2023 (age 77 years).

name: Spirometry
desc: This category contains data on breath spirometry. The participant is asked to record two to three blows (lasting for at least 6 seconds) within a period of about 6 minutes. The computer compares the reproducibility of the first two blows and, if acceptable (defined as a <5% difference in forced volume vital capacity (FVC) & Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1)), will indicate that the third blow is not required.

name: Hand examination
desc: This category contains data on hand examination carried out during the 1999 data collection.

name: Hand grip strength
desc: During the clinic (or home) visit at age 60-64 years study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to have their grip strength assessed.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and broken dynamometers) up to 6 tests of grip strength were performed, 3 in the dominant hand and 3 in the non-dominant hand, using a Nottingham electronic dynamometer.

name: Chair rises
desc: During the clinic (or home) visit at age 60-64 years study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to be timed performing 10 chair rises.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and equipment not available) one test of 10 chair rises was performed.

name: Standing balance
desc: During the clinic (or home) visit at age 60-64 years study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to perform tests of standing balance.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and equipment not available) two tests of standing balance were performed, one with eyes open and one with eyes closed.

name: Timed get up and go
desc: During the clinic (or home) visit at age 60-64 years study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to be timed getting up from a chair, walking 3m, turning around, walking back 3m and sitting back in the chair at their normal pace (i.e. perform a test known as 'timed get up and go').  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and equipment or insufficient space) one test of timed get up and go was performed.  Unlike in other tests participants were able to use walking aids to complete this test.

name: Walk test
desc: During the clinic visit at age 69 years, study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to take part in the walk test.

name: Blood biochemistry

name: NMR metabolomics
desc: NMR metabolic biomarkers generated by Nightingale Health. Data is currently available for Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the study, measuring 251 metabolic biomarkers for EDTA plasma samples from approx 280,000  participants. Metabolic biomarkers were measured from randomly selected EDTA plasma samples (aliquot 3) using a high-throughput NMR-based metabolic biomarker profiling platform developed by Nightingale Health Ltd. The measurements took place between June 2019 and April 2020 (Phase 1) and April 2020 and June 2022 (Phase 2) using eight spectrometers at Nightingale Health, based in Finland. The biomarkers span multiple metabolic pathways, including lipoprotein lipids in 14 subclasses, fatty acids and fatty acid compositions, as well as various low-molecular weight metabolites, such as amino acids, ketone bodies, and glycolysis metabolites quantified in molar concentration units. Previously available data from Phase 1 of the study has been updated as a part of the July 2023 release due to updates in spectrometer recalibration (further information can be found inResource 130). Currently available data is not final and may be updated due to recalibration and normalisation procedures before the project completes.

name: General health questionnaire (GHQ) - screening for psychiatric disorder
desc: The GHQ is a series of questions which act as a screening device for identifying minor psychiatric disorders in the general population. The version used by the NSHD is the GHQ-28: a 28 item scaled version which assesses somatic symptoms, anxiety and insomnia, social dysfunction and severe depression.

name: AD8 Dementia screening interview
desc: This is an eight-item informant interview to differentiate between ageing and dementia. The AD8 was developed as a brief instrument to help discriminate between signs of normal aging and mild dementia. The AD8 contains 8 items that test for memory, orientation, judgment, and function. Cut points are: normal cognition 0-1; impairment in cognition 2 or greater. The AD8 assesses intra-individual change across a variety of cognitive domains compared to previous levels of function and is sensitive to early signs of dementia regardless of etiology.

name: Screening questions for cognitive symptoms
desc: This category contains the screening questions for cognitive symptoms asked in the 2025 postal questionnaire (age 79 years).

name: Present State Examination
desc: This category contains the Present State Examination (PSE) asked in 1982 (age 36 years)

name: Psychiatric Symptom Frequency inventory (PSF)
desc: This category contains the psychiatric symptom frequency inventory scale (PSF; Rodgers, 1994). This was administered by nurses. The PSF is an interview-based scale of symptoms of anxiety and depression over the previous 12 months. The reliability and validity of this measure is reported by Lindelow et al. (1997).

name: Parental bonding instrument (PBI)
desc: This category contains information on the parental bonding instrument. The Parental Bonding Instrument was included on the 1989 self completion questionnaire. Of the 25 items in the scale one was omitted (item 4: Seemed emotionally cold to me), and 5 items were reworded from a negative direction to a positive direction (items 2, 8, 14, 18 and 24). The scale using NSHD was originally created by Bryan Rodgers and used in Reported parental behaviour and adult affective symptoms.

name: Longitudinal latent class analysis for mental health

name: EPIC Physical activity questionnaire

Estimates of PA energy expenditure (PAEE) sedentary behaviour, light (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) were obtained from EPAQ2. Questions were asked in 2006-10 (age 60-64 years)

name: Smoking

Participants were asked questions like,  how many cigarettes they smoked and how long ago they gave up smoking and when they started. Derived smoking pack-years variables are also available. Questions were asked in 1966 (age 20 years), 1971 (age 25 years), 1977 (age 31 years), 1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years), 2014 (age 68 years), 2015 (age 69 years) and 2022 (age 76 years).

The version used by the NSHD is the GHQ-28: a 28 item scaled version which assesses somatic symptoms, anxiety and insomnia, social dysfunction and severe depression. Participants who were unable to answer the questions during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Pulse wave velocity (PWV)
desc: Pulse wave velocity was carried out using a vicorder instrument. Participants who were unable to do the test during the Insight 46 Phase 3 sub-study were asked to do the test when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Pulse wave analysis (PWA)
desc: Pulse wave analysis was carried out using a vicorder instrument. Participants who were unable to do the test during the Insight 46 Phase 3 sub-study were asked to do the test when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Late Gadolinium Enhancement (LGE)
desc: Late gadolinium enhancment (LGE) is a specialised cardiac MRI technique that detects heart muscle scarring, regional fibrosis, and tissue damage. This was only carried out on participants who took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Blood pool
desc: This category contains information about the blood pool. This usually refers to blood within the left ventricular cavity. This can be identified automatically by CVI, or by the user who draws a region of interest around it. Measuring signal intensity of this is needed for quantitative perfusion. This test was done on the 1946 birth cohort participants who took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Quantitative Perfusion
desc: Quantifies myocardial blood flow from perfusion MRI- uses the signal contrast from the qualitative stress perfusion images and derives a quantitative blood flow. This test was done on the 1946 birth cohort participants who took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Heart tissue characteristics
desc: This category contains data on the heart tissue characteristics mapping. This test was done on the 1946 birth cohort participants who took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Economic circumstances
desc: This category contains data on the economic circumstances of the participant such as household income and benefit details, recorded by the 1946 birth cohort participants who took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study. Participants who were unable to do answer the questions during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Spirometry
desc: This category contains data on breath spirometry. The participant is asked to record two to three blows (lasting for at least 6 seconds) within a period of about 6 minutes. The computer compares the reproducibility of the first two blows and, if acceptable (defined as a <5% difference in forced volume vital capacity (FVC) & Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1)), will indicate that the third blow is not required. Participants who were unable to do the test during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Blood pressure
desc: This category contains data on seated blood pressure of the study members who took part in the MyoFit 46 study. Some participants also provided standing blood pressure.

name: Hand grip strength
desc: Study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to have their grip strength assessed.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and broken dynamometers) up to 6 tests of grip strength were performed, 3 in the dominant hand and 3 in the non-dominant hand, using a Nottingham electronic dynamometer. Participants who were unable to do the test during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Chair rises
desc: Study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to be timed performing 10 chair rises.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and equipment not available) one test of 10 chair rises was performed. Participants who were unable to do the test during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Standing balance
desc: Study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to perform tests of standing balance.  If willing and able (reasons for inability included health reasons and equipment not available) two tests of standing balance were performed, one with eyes open and one with eyes closed. Participants who were unable to do the test during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Walk test
desc: Study participants were asked by the attending nurse whether they would be willing to take part in the walk test. Participants who were unable to do the test during the 2023 Home visit were asked to when they took part in the Myofit (2020-2024) sub-study.

name: Reading comprehension (Watts-Vernon)
desc: The Watts-Vernon Reading Test, first given at age 15 years, was re-administered at age 26 years, with an additional 10 items of increased difficulty to avoid a ceiling effect (Rodgers, 1986).

name: Peg placement
desc: The mean peg placement speed, calculated as the overall mean of five trials per hand.

name: Visual memory
desc: A 5-item delayed (20 minutes) picture recall task.

name: Memory (word list memory test)
desc: For each of three trials survey members were shown a list of 15 words at a rate of two seconds each, then were asked to write down as many words recalled as possible.

name: Processing speed
desc: Letter search speed: mean speed for each of the three trials.

name: National audit reading test (NART)
desc: The National Adult Reading Test (NART; Nelson & Willison, 1991). This is a pronunciation test involving 50 irregular words of increasing difficulty, chosen to violate conventional grapheme-phoneme correspondence rules. To pronounce any of the words correctly the respondent must therefore be able to recognise them in their written form rather than rely on intelligent guesswork.  Thus it is effectively a test of knowledge acquisition, although it correlates with full-scale IQ.

name: Verbal fluency
desc: Category fluency was assessed by asking survey members to name as many different animals as possible in 1 minute.  The score is the total number of animals named, allowing anything belonging to the animal kingdom (from amoeba to humans), but not counting repetitions, redundancies (e.g. brown cow, spotted cow) or proper names (e.g. Rover, Kitty).

name: Reaction time
desc: This is a standard manual reaction time (RT) task with visual signal, involving two conditions: 1. Simple, requiring survey members to press one button as quickly as possible following a signal.  Eight practice trials were given, followed by 20 real trials.  To avoid anticipation there was a variable delay (1-3 sec) between each response and the next signal. 2. Choice, requiring survey members to press one of four buttons as quickly as possible corresponding to which of the numbers 1 to 4 appeared in the signal screen.  Eight practice trials were given, followed by 40 real trials.  Note that this condition requires both hands to be functioning.

name: Sensory difficulties
desc: This category contains information if the participant had visual or hearing difficulties during testing.

name: Memory difficulties
desc: This category contains information if the participant had memory difficulties.

name: ACE-III (cognitive state)
desc: This category contains information on the Addenbrooke's Cognition Examination (ACE).

name: Finger tapping
desc: The finger tapping test involved the participants tapping a machine lever as many times as possible in ten seconds, once with each index finger.

name: Six day word recall
desc: During the home visit, the participant were shown a list of words and was asked several times to write down all the words that they could remember. After 6 days, participant is asked: When I tell you to start, I would like you to write down all the words you can remember now on the lines provided. I will give you one minute to do this – I will tell you when to start and stop.

name: Envelope test
desc: The envelope test was carried out in the 1999 data collection. Participant was asked to write an address on the envelope and write their initials on the back. After a few minutes it was checked whether they remembered to put their intials on the envelope.

name: Memory test
desc: Asked participant during the 1989 data collection that do they remember if they were examined by the nurse and had some physical measurements taken, such as: pulse, blood pressure, lung function, height, weight, arm/chest/abdominal circumference.

name: Bone size, mineral and density by DXA
desc: Bone composition results derived from  DXA measurements.

name: Body composition by DXA
desc: Body composition results derived from DXA measurements.

name: Pulse wave analysis (PWA)
desc: Pulse wave analysis and blood pressure measurement was carried out using a vicorder instrument.

name: Pulse wave velocity (PWV)
desc: Pulse wave velocity was carried out using a vicorder instrument.

name: Cardiac MRI
desc: Derived phenotypes of cardiac and aortic structure and function.

name: Echocardiogram
desc: This category contains information from the echocardiogram done by the 1946 birth cohort participants.

name: Carotid ultrasound
desc: Ultrasound scan of carotid artery.

name: Body size measures
desc: This category contains data on body composition measures that were taken manually i.e. weight, standing and sitting height, body mass index (BMI) and abdominal/hip/chest/arm circumference. Measures were taken from birth to adulthood.

name: Heart rate variability
desc: This category contains information on heart rate variability.

name: Metabolon - Original scores
desc: Metabolon data collected from the blood samples of the 1946 birth cohort participants. These variables are the original scores with no imputation.

name: Metabolon - Imputed scores
desc: Metabolon data collected from the blood samples of the 1946 birth cohort participants. The missing values were imputed using the minimum value and the scale adjusted for the median to be 1.

name: Raw medication taken in the last 24 hours
desc: This category contains information about the raw medication (BNF codes), taken 24 hours before the nurse visit at 2006-10 (age 60-64 years).

name: Derived medication taken in the last 24 hours
desc: This category contains information about derived medication variables taken 24 hours before the nurse visit at 2006-10 (age 60-64 years).

name: Regular medication including BNF codes and names of drugs
desc: This category contains information about the regular medication, raw BNF codes,  taken by the participant.

name: Regular medication - Derived variables
desc: This category contains information about the regular medication, derived,  taken by the participant.

name: Heart and circulatory conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on whether the participant had any heart or circulatory conditions i.e. heart attacks, heart failure, pulmonary embolism, strokes and varicose veins or blood pressure problems. Discomfort in the leg and chest were also recorded. Rose angina variables were derived. Questions were asked in  1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years), 2014 (age 68 years), 2015 (age 69 years), 2022 (age 76 years) and 2025 (age 79 years).

name: Cancer
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on cancer (self reported). Data was collected in 1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years) and 2015 (age 69 years). Information includes ICD codes and age of cancer, whether medicine was prescribed.

name: Respiratory conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on whether the participant has and respiratory conditions i.e chronic lung disease, COPD, emphysema, asthma, bronchitis and hayfever. They were also asked if they were prescribed medication. CLS asthma harmonisation dataset is also included). Questions were asked in 1948 (age 2 years), 1952 (age 6 years), 1953 (age 7 years), 1957 (age 11 years), 1961 (age 15 years), 1966 (age 20 years), 1971 (age 25 years), 1977 (age 31 years), 1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years), 2014 (age 68 years), 2015 (age 69 years), 2020-21 (covid), 2022 (age 76 years), 2023 (age 77 years) and 2025 (age 79 years).

name: Musculoskeletal system conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on rheumatoid arthiritis, osteoarthiritis,  osteoporosis and backache which includes sciatica.

name: Digestive and genitourinary system conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on digestive and genitourinary conditions, such as issues with stomach, gall bladder, gums and mouth, liver and hernia. It also includes details about constipation and bowel problems. Kidney, bladder infections and incontinence were also added for the genitourinary conditions.

name: Endocrine and metabolic conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on whether the participant has any endocrine and metabolic conditions asked in 1982 (age 36 years), 1989 (age 43 years), 1999 (age 53 years), 2006-10 (age 60-64 years), 2014 (age 68 years), 2015 (age 69 years) and 2025 (age 79 years). Data collected includes the type of diabetes, how it is being controlled and the date of diagnosis. At age 60-64 years GP validation was also carried out. The CLS harmonisation dataset which also includes the covid questionnaires 2020-2022 is also included.

name: Nervous system conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on nervous system conditions, such as epilepsy, parkinsons, myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), headache and migraines.

name: Mental and behavioural conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on mental and behavioural conditions, such as depression, delirium, memory and cognitive impairment.

name: Eye conditions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on eye conditions, such as cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration and laser treatment for diabetic retinopathy.

name: Clinical disorders (Derived at age 60-64 years)
desc: This category contains the derived clinical disorder variables in 2006-10 (at age 60-64 years). These include cardio and cerebo-vascular disease, hypertension, raised cholesterol, renal impairment, diabetes, obesity, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, anaemia, respiratory disease, liver disease, psychiatric problems, cancer, atrial fibrillation on ECG and osteporosis.

name: Other medical conditions
desc: This category contains data on all other medical conditions the participant reported which have not been classified in another category.

name: Hospital in-patient admissions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on hospital admitted patient tests and treatments. This includes ECG, X-ray, angiogram, angioplasty and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) operation questions.

name: Hospital out-patient admissions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on hospital out-patient admissions. This is for treatments and surgery at the hospital where the participant went home the same day and did not spend a night in hospital.

name: Childhood health examination
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on childhood health examination mainly carried out by the doctor i.e. pulse, nassal pasages, throat and tonsils, lungs, heart, abdomen etc. Speech, ears, eyes and handedness were aslo assessed.

name: Childhood health
desc: This category contains data on childhood health, such as infectious diseases or feeling sick.

name: Childhood development
desc: This category contains data on developmental milestones and puberty.

name: Job and occupational histories (1961-1999)
desc: The category includes information on jobs reported by cohort members at one of eight surveys conducted between the ages of 16 and 53. The jobs are organised into chronological order using reported or inferred job start dates in conjunction with the interview dates when the job episodes were collected. Information on the occupation of each job has been re-coded from SOC60, SOC70 and SOC80 codes into SOC90 codes. The dataset is designed for the analysis of changes in occupational status over time. It does not include information on spells of unemployment or economic inactivity. This work forms part of the ESRC Gender Network Grant, Project 1 ‘Changing occupational careers of men and women’, Reference: RES-225-25-2001.

name: Social class (1972-1999)
desc: This category contains dervied social class variables using own and partner’s occupation asked at 26, 36, 43 and 53 years. Childhood social class was derived from Father's occupation.

name: EPIC Physical activity questionnaire - derived variables
desc: This category contains derived data from the EPAQ2, which assessed self-report physical activity in four domains (leisure time, occupation, transportation and domestic life). Estimates of PA energy expenditure (PAEE) sedentary behaviour, light (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) were obtained from EPAQ2. Questions were asked in 2006-10 (age 60-64 years)

name: EPIC Physical activity questionnaire - raw variables
desc: This category contains raw data from the EPAQ2, which assessed self-report physical activity in four domains (leisure time, occupation, transportation and domestic life). Estimates of PA energy expenditure (PAEE) sedentary behaviour, light (LPA) and moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA) were obtained from EPAQ2.

name: Type of visit
desc: This category contains information about type of visit (remote or in-person) for Insight46 phase 2, as some visits were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic

name: Education
desc: This category contains data from the Insight46 sub-study on the education level of the participant.This updates previously colleted NSHD education data.

name: Brain volumes
desc: This category contains variables related to the brain volumes (cross-sectional and longitudinal measures) parcellated from T1 MRI (phases 1 and 2) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: White matter hyperintsity (WMH) volumes
desc: This category contains variables related to the white matter hyperintensity volumnes generated using the Bayesian Model Seletion (BaMoS) pipeline from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Normal appearing white matter (NAWM)
desc: This category contains variables related to the normal appearing white matter (NAWM) diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) parameters indexing microstructural integrity from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Cortical thickness
desc: This category contains variables related to the cortical thickness assessed using Freesurfer from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Brain age
desc: This category contains variables related to the derived brain-predicted age from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Amyloid data
desc: This category contains variables related to the cross-sectional beta-amyloid status (phase 1); longitudinal beta-amyloid status, standard uptake value ratios (SUVRs), and centiloid values (phases 1 and 2) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Blood pressure
desc: This category contains information on blood pressure measurements collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Anthropometry
desc: This category contains information on the type of body composition measures that were performed in the Insight46  sub-study, including height, weight, body mass index (BMI) and impedance.

name: Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS)
desc: This category contains information on the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) in the Insight46  sub-study.

name: Hearing test
desc: This category contains information on the Pure tone audiometry and words presented against background noise collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Smell test
desc: This category contains information on the University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification test collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Stepper test
desc: This category contains information on the six-minute self-paced stepper test. This is administered to assess the participants exercise capacity and the effects of exercise on physiological measures including blood pressure and heart rate.

name: Bradykinesia Akinesia Incoordination (BRAIN) Tap Test
desc: This category contains information on the online keyboard tapping test to assess upper limb motor function collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Gait assessment
desc: This category contains information on the Instrumented 10 metre gait assessment collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Blood biochemistry
desc: This category contains information on key biochemistry markers from the blood samples collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Blood biomarkers
desc: This category contains measurements in plasma or serum of neurofilament light (NFL), total tau, amyloid-beta 40, amyloid-beta 42, ptau-181 (phase 1), and ptau-217 (phases 1 and 2)

name: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers
desc: This category contains measurements in CSF of amyloid-beta 40, amyloid-beta 42, ptau 181, total tau, ptau-217 collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Genotype
desc: This category contains the ApoE allele status collected as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Family history of neurological disorder
desc: This category contains data on the self-reported history of neurological disorder in parents and siblings of the participant in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Personal history of neurological disorder
desc: This category contains information on self-reported personal history of neurological disoder; consensus assessment of mild cognitive impairment and dementia of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Medications
desc: This category contains information on medications taken in last 24 hours (phases 1 and 2) and further categorization of vascular medications of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Head injury
desc: This category contains information on history of head injury of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Delirium
desc: This category contains information on Instances of delirium of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Dental health
desc: This category contains information about dental health of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Sleep
desc: This category contains questions about activing out dreams (phase 1); several validated sleep questionnaires (phase 2): Epworth Sleepiness Questionnaire, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder Screening Questionnaire (RBDSQ) of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Anxiety
desc: This category contains information about the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Negative thinking
desc: This category contains information about the Perseverative Thinking Questionnaire (PTQ) of the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Informant interviews
desc: This category contains information about the AD8 dementia screening interview and Clinical Dementia Rating Scale carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Mini-mental state examination
desc: This category contains information relating  to the Test of five areas of cognitive function - orientation, registration, attention and calculation, recall, and language carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Reaction time
desc: This category contains information about the Choice Reaction Time (RT) and Response Inhibition tasks carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Fluid intelligence and reasoning
desc: This category contains information about the Matrix Reasoning test carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Symbol digit substitution
desc: This category contains information about the Digit-Symbol Substitution Test from the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale-Revised (WAIS-R) carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Picture vocabulary
desc: This category contains information about the Graded naming tests (GNT) carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Visuomotor performance
desc: This category contains information about the Circle tracing and serial subtraction task carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Visual short-term memory
desc: This category contains information about the “What was where?” visual short-term memory binding test carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Associative episodic memory
desc: This category contains information about the Face-Name test (FNAME-12) carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Logical memory
desc: This category contains information about the Logical Memory IIa immediate and delayed recall from the Wechsler Memory Scale (WMS) carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Visuo-constructional ability and visual memory
desc: This category contains information about the Adult Memory and Information Processing Battery (AMIPB) complex figure drawing carried out by the participants in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC)
desc: This category contains the serviced Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC) score

name: Empatica
desc: This category contains the information from the empatica device worn during the Insight 46 study

name: Echocardiogram - 3D reports
desc: This category contains information from the echocardiogram 3D reports done by the 1946 participants as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Echocardiogram - 2D reports
desc: This category contains information from the echocardiogram 2D reports done by the 1946 participants as part of the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Blood biochemistry
desc: A range of key biochemistry markers were measured in the blood samples collected at the Myofit sub-study (2020-2024).

name: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT)
desc: This category contains information from the carotid intima-media thickness test done by the 1946 birth cohort participants.

name: Medication derivations done longitudinally
desc: This category contains information about the regular medication taken by the participant - derived across the data collections.

name: Medication derivations at data collection level (cross-sectional)
desc: This category contains information about the regular medication taken by the participant - derived at the data collection level.

name: Chest pain or heart disease admissions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on hospital admitted patient tests and treatments. This includes ECG, X-ray, angiogram, angioplasty and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) operation questions.

name: All other hospital admissions
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on all other hospital admitted patient tests and treatments.

name: Hospital admissions validated against hospital records
desc: This category contains data from the questionnaires on all self-reported hospital admitted patient validated against hospital records at age 60-64 years.

name: Brain volumes - Cross-sectional
desc: This category contains variables related to the brain volumes (cross-sectional) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Brain volumes - Longitudinal (phase 1 and 2)
desc: This category contains variables related to the brain volumes (longitudinal measures) parcellated from T1 MRI (phases 1 and 2) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: White matter hyperintsity (WMH) volumes - Cross-sectional
desc: This category contains the cross-sectional variables related to the white matter hyperintensity volumnes generated using the Bayesian Model Seletion (BaMoS) pipeline from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: White matter hyperintsity (WMH) volumes - Longitudinal (phase 1 and 2)
desc: This category contains the longitudinal (phase 1 and 2 only) variables related to the white matter hyperintensity volumnes generated using the Bayesian Model Seletion (BaMoS) pipeline from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Cross-sectional beta-amyloid status (phase 1)
desc: This category contains variables related to the cross-sectional beta-amyloid status (phase 1) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Longitudinal beta-amyloid status (phase 1 and 2)
desc: This category contains variables related to the longitudinal beta-amyloid status, standard uptake value ratios (SUVRs), and centiloid values (phases 1 and 2) from the MRI brain imaging carried out on the participants taking part in the Insight46 sub-study.

name: Body size measures
desc: This category contains information on the type of body composition measures that were performed in the Insight46  sub-study, including height, weight, body mass index (BMI).

name: Body composition by impedance
desc: This category contains data on whole body bio-impedance measures using Tanita body composition analyser (i.e. basal metabolic rate, body tape, height, weight, body fat mass, body fat percentage, fat free mass, water mass and impendance for the right arm, right leg, left arm, left leg, and trunk)
